finding: The tested wall and mixing settings do not explain the main Test 6A G2 discrepancy. With free-slip walls, G2 speed RMSE is 0.821976 m/s without mixing and 0.821925 m/s with Cs=0.1. Adding Cw=0.01 at the throat and obstruction changes it to 0.819115 m/s without mixing and 0.817577 m/s with mixing. Extending the same coefficient to every exterior wall gives 0.818514 m/s without mixing, a reduction of only 0.42% relative to free slip. Wall-only effects are mixed across the level and speed records; with mixing, the selected throat and obstruction walls produce small reductions in all five recovered-series RMSEs. The wall-energy ledger confirms that traction was applied, but the G2 speed and level disagreement remains substantial. These results do not justify treating these settings as a correction to the benchmark or changing the off/free-slip defaults. All 9 configurations completed their prescribed durations and passed the saved-depth and water-balance checks.
qualification: The coefficients were declared diagnostic values, not measured or fitted wall roughness. The all-wall coverage control was added after the regional runs showed little G2 change, retaining the same coefficient. Errors cover only visibility-selected digitized UCL markers, with missing G6 observations and unknown instrument uncertainty; the small changes do not establish a physical cause. Original measurements, drawing-versus-DEM geometry qualification, mesh/timestep and probe-sampling sensitivity, and wall-material evidence are still needed. Test 6B uses the chosen elevation scaling of 20 and has no independent measured reference; its numerical checks cannot establish physical accuracy.
